hook: Nick Frosst studied computer science and cognitive science at the University of Toronto, working with researchers including John Tsotsos, Sanja Fidler and Jimmy Ba. He became the first employee of Geoffrey Hinton's Google Brain lab in Toronto, where he spent three years researching capsule networks, adversarial examples and model explainability. During that time he co-authored "Dynamic Routing Between Capsules" with Sara Sabour and Geoffrey Hinton, a widely cited paper proposing an alternative to standard convolutional pooling. In 2019 he left Google to co-found Cohere with Aidan Gomez and Ivan Zhang, building an enterprise-focused large language model company. Alongside his machine learning career, Frosst is also an active musician.
